about: Design and color guidance: WCAG contrast, filament colors as makers publish them, harmony rules, edges and text sizes.

entries.note: SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA, normal text.
entries.quote: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for the following:
entries.source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

entries.note: SC 1.4.3 large-scale text exception, Level AA.
entries.quote: Large-scale text and images of large-scale text have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1;
entries.source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

entries.note: Large scale means at least 18 pt regular or 14 pt bold.
entries.quote: with at least 18 point or 14 point bold or font size that would yield equivalent size for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (CJK) fonts
entries.source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

entries.note: Linearize each sRGB channel first: c = c8bit/255; if c <= 0.04045 then c/12.92 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4. The current WCAG 2.2 text uses 0.04045 (older copies said 0.03928).
entries.quote: For the sRGB colorspace, the relative luminance of a color is defined as L = 0.2126 * R + 0.7152 * G + 0.0722 * B where R , G and B are defined as: if RsRGB <= 0.04045 then R = RsRGB/12.92 else R = ((RsRGB+0.055)/1.055) ^ 2.4
entries.source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

entries.note: L1 is the lighter color luminance, L2 the darker. Range 1 to 21.
entries.quote: (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), where L1 is the relative luminance of the lighter of the colors, and L2 is the relative luminance of the darker of the colors. Note 1 Contrast ratios can range from 1 to 21 (commonly written 1:1 to 21:1).
entries.source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

entries.value: Two hues opposite each other on the color wheel; high contrast.
entries.quote: A complementary color scheme consists of two colors that sit opposite each other on the color wheel.
entries.source: What is Color Harmony? | IxDF (Interaction Design Foundation)

entries.value: Three hues next to each other on the color wheel; calm, cohesive.
entries.quote: An analogous color scheme involves three adjacent colors on the color wheel.
entries.source: What is Color Harmony? | IxDF (Interaction Design Foundation)

entries.value: Three hues evenly spaced, 120 degrees apart, on the color wheel.
entries.quote: A triadic color scheme consists of three colors spaced evenly around the color wheel. To identify these colors, you can place an equilateral triangle on the wheel; each corner will point to a color 120° apart from the others.
entries.source: What is Color Harmony? | IxDF (Interaction Design Foundation)

entries.value: A base hue plus the two hues adjacent to its complement; softer than complementary.
entries.quote: In split-complementary color schemes, designers blend the principles of complementary and analogous colors. They select the complementary color to their primary and then include the adjacent colors on the color wheel.
entries.source: What is Color Harmony? | IxDF (Interaction Design Foundation)

entries.note: Bed-facing edges: a fillet makes a very steep overhang; use a chamfer when finish matters.
entries.quote: If oriented towards the print bed, fillets create a very steep overhang, which negatively affects the surface of the object. For this reason, use chamfer instead if a perfect part finish is a priority.
entries.source: Modeling with 3D printing in mind | Prusa Knowledge Base

entries.note: Chamfer or radius every edge touching the build plate (elephant foot, part removal).
entries.quote: Key design consideration: If assembly or overall dimensions are critical to the function of an FDM part, include a 45° chamfer or radius on all edges touching the build plate.
entries.source: How to design parts for FDM 3D printing | Protolabs Network (Hubs)

entries.note: FDM vertical corners can never be sharper than the nozzle radius.
entries.quote: Because FDM printing nozzles are circular, corners and edges have a radius equal to the nozzle size. This means that these features are never perfectly square.
entries.source: How to design parts for FDM 3D printing | Protolabs Network (Hubs)

entries.note: Pins under 5 mm diameter get a small fillet at the base (stress concentration).
entries.quote: Key design consideration: If your design contains pins smaller than 5mm in diameter, add a small fillet at the base of the pin.
entries.source: How to design parts for FDM 3D printing | Protolabs Network (Hubs)

entries.note: Fillets reduce stress concentration; sharp edges concentrate stress.
entries.quote: Although fillets are not necessary in FDM parts, they can reduce stress concentrations and increase the overall strength of the part.
entries.source: Design Guide FDM, Stratasys Direct (PDF, July 2025)

entries.note: Keeps wall thickness constant around a bend.
entries.quote: Design fillets with an outer radius equal to the inner radius plus the wall thickness to maintain consistent thickness.
entries.source: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) Design Guidelines, Stratasys Direct (2017 PDF)

entries.note: Lead a bed-facing fillet with a 45 degree chamfer of 0.5858 x the fillet radius (half is close enough).
entries.quote: In order to fix this issue, use a 45 degree chamfer to start the fillet, then create the fillet off of that. The resulting fillet is never any steeper than 45 degrees and prints without warping or other artifacts. A chamfer half your fillet radius is usually close enough.
entries.source: FDM 3D Printing Tips for Better Prototypes | StarFish Medical

entries.note: Hand-held items are squeezed, so NASA applies the fixed-equipment rounding table (Table 9.3-1) to them.
entries.quote: Although hand-held items are loose, they are squeezed, and forces can be high. Therefore, hand-held items are to meet the edge and corner rounding requirements of fixed items
entries.source: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2, Revision F (approved 2026-07-14)

entries.note: NASA Table 9.3-1: material thickness 3.0 mm <= t < 6.5 mm: min edge radius 1.5 mm, min corner radius 6.5 mm.
entries.source: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2, Revision F (approved 2026-07-14)

entries.note: NASA Table 9.3-1: material thickness 6.5 mm <= t <= 25 mm: min edge radius 3.0 mm, min corner radius 13 mm.
entries.source: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2, Revision F (approved 2026-07-14)

entries.note: NASA Table 9.3-1: smallest required corner radius for any hand-held or fixed item is 6.5 mm (13 mm when t >= 6.5 mm).
entries.quote: 0.5 mm ≤ t < 3.0 mm 6.5 mm Full radius (0.02 in ≤ t < 0.12 in) (0.26 in)
entries.source: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2, Revision F (approved 2026-07-14)

entries.note: Desktop/service FDM minimum raised height.
entries.quote: Such features should be designed at least 0.3mm in height.
entries.source: Design Guide: FDM 3D Printing | HLH Rapid

entries.quote: Engraved details should be at least 0.5mm deep and 0.5mm wide.
entries.source: Design Guide: FDM 3D Printing | HLH Rapid

entries.note: Minimum stroke width for engraved features.
entries.quote: Engraved details should be at least 0.5mm deep and 0.5mm wide.
entries.source: Design Guide: FDM 3D Printing | HLH Rapid

entries.note: Industrial FDM (PC-ISO): engraved letters 1 mm line, 0.3 mm deep.
entries.quote: For engraved text or surface details, we recommend letters with a minimum line thickness of 1 mm and a depth of 0.3 mm.
entries.source: PC-ISO design guide | Materialise (industrial FDM)

entries.note: Industrial FDM (PC-ISO): embossed letters 2.5 mm line, 0.5 mm high. Engraved preferred over embossed.
entries.quote: For embossed text and surface details, we recommend that letters have a line thickness of at least 2.5 mm and a depth of at least 0.5 mm.
entries.source: PC-ISO design guide | Materialise (industrial FDM)

entries.note: University guide: 1.0 mm embossed minimum, 14 pt minimum font; legibility depends on the font.
entries.quote: Embossed & Engraved Details Features on the model that are raised or recessed below the model surface. Min. 1.0[mm] embossed Min. Font 14pt
entries.source: Design Guideline FDM | University of Zurich AMF (PDF)
entries.cite: University of Zurich FDM design guideline

entries.quote: Min. Font 14pt
entries.source: Design Guideline FDM | University of Zurich AMF (PDF)
entries.cite: University of Zurich FDM design guideline

entries.note: Bold monospace (Courier New) at 24 pt or larger prints legibly regardless of material, layer height and orientation.
entries.quote: We recommend a monospaced fonts - Courier New, in a bold font with 24+ point styling.
entries.source: Design Guide FDM, Stratasys Direct (PDF, July 2025)

entries.note: Narrowest stroke at least the nozzle width; under about 0.5 mm fails with a 0.4 mm nozzle. Maker blog, rule of thumb.
entries.quote: Stroke thickness. The narrowest part of any letter should be at least as wide as your nozzle - ideally more. With a common 0.4 mm nozzle, printing strokes under about half a millimeter is asking for trouble.
entries.source: 3D Printing Text and Logos: How to Emboss, Engrave, and Print Clean Details | Sovol

entries.note: ADA 703.5.5: 5/8 in (16 mm) minimum uppercase I height for viewing distance under 72 in (1830 mm), mounted 40 to 70 in high.
entries.quote: less than 72 inches (1830 mm) 5/8 inch (16 mm)
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.note: ADA 703.5.5: add 1/8 in (3.2 mm) per foot of viewing distance beyond 72 in.
entries.quote: 5/8 inch (16 mm), plus 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) per foot (305 mm) of viewing distance above 72 inches (1830 mm)
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.note: ADA 703.5.7 visual character stroke.
entries.quote: Stroke thickness of the uppercase letter “I” shall be 10 percent minimum and 30 percent maximum of the height of the character.
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.note: ADA 703.2.1 raised (tactile) characters: 1/32 in (0.8 mm) minimum.
entries.quote: Raised characters shall be 1/32 inch (0.8 mm) minimum above their background.
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.note: ADA 703.2.5 raised characters 5/8 in (16 mm) to 2 in (51 mm), uppercase sans serif.
entries.quote: Character height measured vertically from the baseline of the character shall be 5/8 inch (16 mm) minimum and 2 inches (51 mm) maximum based on the height of the uppercase letter “I”.
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.quote: Stroke thickness of the uppercase letter “I” shall be 15 percent maximum of the height of the character.
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov

entries.value: light on dark or dark on light
entries.note: ADA 703.5.1, non-glare finish.
entries.quote: Characters and their background shall have a non-glare finish. Characters shall contrast with their background with either light characters on a dark background or dark characters on a light background.
entries.source: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design | ADA.gov
